paragraphs.text: And the whole company of them rose up, and brought him before Pilate.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἀναστὰν ἅπαν τὸ πλῆθος αὐτῶν ἤγαγον αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τὸν Πιλᾶτον.
paragraphs.translit: Kai anastan hapan to plēthos autōn ēgagon auton epi ton Pilaton.

paragraphs.text: And they began to accuse him, saying, We found this man perverting our nation, and forbidding to give tribute to Caesar, and saying that he himself is Christ a king.
paragraphs.original: ἤρξαντο δὲ κατηγορεῖν αὐτοῦ λέγοντες· Τοῦτον εὕραμεν διαστρέφοντα τὸ ἔθνος ἡμῶν καὶ κωλύοντα φόρους Καίσαρι διδόναι καὶ λέγοντα αὑτὸν χριστὸν βασιλέα εἶναι.
paragraphs.translit: ērxanto de katēgorein autou legontes· Touton heuramen diastrephonta to ethnos hēmōn kai kōlyonta phorous Kaisari didonai kai legonta hauton christon basilea einai.

paragraphs.text: And Pilate asked him, saying, Art thou the King of the Jews? And he answered him and said, Thou sayest.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος ἠρώτησεν αὐτὸν λέγων· Σὺ εἶ ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων; ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς αὐτῷ ἔφη· Σὺ λέγεις.
paragraphs.translit: ho de Pilatos ērōtēsen auton legōn· Sy ei ho basileus tōn Ioudaiōn; ho de apokritheis autō ephē· Sy legeis.

paragraphs.text: And Pilate said unto the chief priests and the multitudes, I find no fault in this man.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος εἶπεν πρὸς τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ τοὺς ὄχλους· Οὐδὲν εὑρίσκω αἴτιον ἐν τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ τούτῳ.
paragraphs.translit: ho de Pilatos eipen pros tous archiereis kai tous ochlous· Ouden heuriskō aition en tō anthrōpō toutō.

paragraphs.text: But they were the more urgent, saying, He stirreth up the people, teaching throughout all Judaea, and beginning from Galilee even unto this place.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ ἐπίσχυον λέγοντες ὅτι Ἀνασείει τὸν λαὸν διδάσκων καθʼ ὅλης τῆς Ἰουδαίας, καὶ ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας ἕως ὧδε.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de epischyon legontes hoti Anaseiei ton laon didaskōn kathʼ holēs tēs Ioudaias, kai arxamenos apo tēs Galilaias heōs hōde.

paragraphs.text: But when Pilate heard it, he asked whether the man were a Galilaean.
paragraphs.original: Πιλᾶτος δὲ ἀκούσας ἐπηρώτησεν εἰ ὁ ἄνθρωπος Γαλιλαῖός ἐστιν,
paragraphs.translit: Pilatos de akousas epērōtēsen ei ho anthrōpos Galilaios estin,

paragraphs.text: And when he knew that he was of Herod`s jurisdiction, he sent him unto Herod, who himself also was at Jerusalem in these days.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐπιγνοὺς ὅτι ἐκ τῆς ἐξουσίας Ἡρῴδου ἐστὶν ἀνέπεμψεν αὐτὸν πρὸς Ἡρῴδην, ὄντα καὶ αὐτὸν ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις ἐν ταύταις ταῖς ἡμέραις.
paragraphs.translit: kai epignous hoti ek tēs exousias Hērōdou estin anepempsen auton pros Hērōdēn, onta kai auton en Hierosolymois en tautais tais hēmerais.

paragraphs.text: Now when Herod saw Jesus, he was exceeding glad: for he was of a long time desirous to see him, because he had heard concerning him; and he hoped to see some miracle done by him.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Ἡρῴδης ἰδὼν τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐχάρη λίαν, ἦν γὰρ ἐξ ἱκανῶν χρόνων θέλων ἰδεῖν αὐτὸν διὰ τὸ ἀκούειν περὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἤλπιζέν τι σημεῖον ἰδεῖν ὑπʼ αὐτοῦ γινόμενον.
paragraphs.translit: ho de Hērōdēs idōn ton Iēsoun echarē lian, ēn gar ex hikanōn chronōn thelōn idein auton dia to akouein peri autou, kai ēlpizen ti sēmeion idein hypʼ autou ginomenon.

paragraphs.text: And he questioned him in many words; but he answered him nothing.
paragraphs.original: ἐπηρώτα δὲ αὐτὸν ἐν λόγοις ἱκανοῖς· αὐτὸς δὲ οὐδὲν ἀπεκρίνατο αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: epērōta de auton en logois hikanois· autos de ouden apekrinato autō.

paragraphs.text: And the chief priests and the scribes stood, vehemently accusing him.
paragraphs.original: εἱστήκεισαν δὲ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς εὐτόνως κατηγοροῦντες αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: heistēkeisan de hoi archiereis kai hoi grammateis eutonōs katēgorountes autou.

paragraphs.text: And Herod with his soldiers set him at nought, and mocked him, and arraying him in gorgeous apparel sent him back to Pilate.
paragraphs.original: ἐξουθενήσας δὲ αὐτὸν καὶ ὁ Ἡρῴδης σὺν τοῖς στρατεύμασιν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐμπαίξας περιβαλὼν ἐσθῆτα λαμπρὰν ἀνέπεμψεν αὐτὸν τῷ Πιλάτῳ.
paragraphs.translit: exouthenēsas de auton kai ho Hērōdēs syn tois strateumasin autou kai empaixas peribalōn esthēta lampran anepempsen auton tō Pilatō.

paragraphs.text: And Herod and Pilate became friends with each other that very day: for before they were at enmity between themselves.
paragraphs.original: ἐγένοντο δὲ φίλοι ὅ τε Ἡρῴδης καὶ ὁ Πιλᾶτος ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ μετʼ ἀλλήλων· προϋπῆρχον γὰρ ἐν ἔχθρᾳ ὄντες πρὸς αὑτούς.
paragraphs.translit: egenonto de philoi ho te Hērōdēs kai ho Pilatos en autē tē hēmera metʼ allēlōn· proupērchon gar en echthra ontes pros hautous.

paragraphs.text: And Pilate called together the chief priests and the rulers and the people,
paragraphs.original: Πιλᾶτος δὲ συγκαλεσάμενος τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ τοὺς ἄρχοντας καὶ τὸν λαὸν
paragraphs.translit: Pilatos de synkalesamenos tous archiereis kai tous archontas kai ton laon

paragraphs.text: and said unto them, Ye brought unto me this man, as one that perverteth the people: and behold, I having examined him before you, found no fault in this man touching those things whereof ye accuse him:
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Προσηνέγκατέ μοι τὸν ἄνθρωπον τοῦτον ὡς ἀποστρέφοντα τὸν λαόν, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ἐνώπιον ὑμῶν ἀνακρίνας οὐθὲν εὗρον ἐν τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ τούτῳ αἴτιον ὧν κατηγορεῖτε κατʼ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: eipen pros autous· Prosēnenkate moi ton anthrōpon touton hōs apostrephonta ton laon, kai idou egō enōpion hymōn anakrinas outhen heuron en tō anthrōpō toutō aition hōn katēgoreite katʼ autou.

paragraphs.text: no, nor yet Herod: for he sent him back unto us; and behold, nothing worthy of death hath been done by him.
paragraphs.original: ἀλλʼ οὐδὲ Ἡρῴδης, ἀνέπεμψεν γὰρ αὐτὸν πρὸς ἡμᾶς· καὶ ἰδοὺ οὐδὲν ἄξιον θανάτου ἐστὶν πεπραγμένον αὐτῷ·
paragraphs.translit: allʼ oude Hērōdēs, anepempsen gar auton pros hēmas· kai idou ouden axion thanatou estin pepragmenon autō·

paragraphs.text: I will therefore chastise him, and release him.
paragraphs.original: παιδεύσας οὖν αὐτὸν ἀπολύσω.
paragraphs.translit: paideusas oun auton apolysō.

paragraphs.text: [Now he must needs release unto them at the feast one prisoner.]
But they cried out all together, saying, Away with this man, and release unto us Barabbas: --
paragraphs.original: Ἀνέκραγον δὲ παμπληθεὶ λέγοντες· Αἶρε τοῦτον, ἀπόλυσον δὲ ἡμῖν τὸν Βαραββᾶν·
paragraphs.translit: Anekragon de pamplēthei legontes· Aire touton, apolyson de hēmin ton Barabban·

paragraphs.text: one who for a certain insurrection made in the city, and for murder, was cast into prison.
paragraphs.original: ὅστις ἦν διὰ στάσιν τινὰ γενομένην ἐν τῇ πόλει καὶ φόνον βληθεὶς ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ.
paragraphs.translit: hostis ēn dia stasin tina genomenēn en tē polei kai phonon blētheis en tē phylakē.

paragraphs.text: And Pilate spake unto them again, desiring to release Jesus;
paragraphs.original: πάλιν δὲ ὁ Πιλᾶτος προσεφώνησεν, θέλων ἀπολῦσαι τὸν Ἰησοῦν.
paragraphs.translit: palin de ho Pilatos prosephōnēsen, thelōn apolysai ton Iēsoun.

paragraphs.text: but they shouted, saying, Crucify, crucify him.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ ἐπεφώνουν λέγοντες· Σταύρου σταύρου αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de epephōnoun legontes· Staurou staurou auton.

paragraphs.text: And he said unto them the third time, Why, what evil hath this man done? I have found no cause of death in him: I will therefore chastise him and release him.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ τρίτον εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Τί γὰρ κακὸν ἐποίησεν οὗτος; οὐδὲν αἴτιον θανάτου εὗρον ἐν αὐτῷ· παιδεύσας οὖν αὐτὸν ἀπολύσω.
paragraphs.translit: ho de triton eipen pros autous· Ti gar kakon epoiēsen houtos; ouden aition thanatou heuron en autō· paideusas oun auton apolysō.

paragraphs.text: But they were urgent with loud voices, asking that he might be crucified. And their voices prevailed.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ ἐπέκειντο φωναῖς μεγάλαις αἰτούμενοι αὐτὸν σταυρωθῆναι, καὶ κατίσχυον αἱ φωναὶ αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de epekeinto phōnais megalais aitoumenoi auton staurōthēnai, kai katischyon hai phōnai autōn.

paragraphs.text: And Pilate gave sentence that what they asked for should be done.
paragraphs.original: καὶ Πιλᾶτος ἐπέκρινεν γενέσθαι τὸ αἴτημα αὐτῶν·
paragraphs.translit: kai Pilatos epekrinen genesthai to aitēma autōn·

paragraphs.text: And he released him that for insurrection and murder had been cast into prison, whom they asked for; but Jesus he delivered up to their will.
paragraphs.original: ἀπέλυσεν δὲ τὸν διὰ στάσιν καὶ φόνον βεβλημένον εἰς φυλακὴν ὃν ᾐτοῦντο, τὸν δὲ Ἰησοῦν παρέδωκεν τῷ θελήματι αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: apelysen de ton dia stasin kai phonon beblēmenon eis phylakēn hon ētounto, ton de Iēsoun paredōken tō thelēmati autōn.

paragraphs.text: And when they led him away, they laid hold upon one Simon of Cyrene, coming from the country, and laid on him the cross, to bear it after Jesus.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ὡς ἀπήγαγον αὐτόν, ἐπιλαβόμενοι Σίμωνά τινα Κυρηναῖον ἐρχόμενον ἀπʼ ἀγροῦ ἐπέθηκαν αὐτῷ τὸν σταυρὸν φέρειν ὄπισθεν τοῦ Ἰησοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: Kai hōs apēgagon auton, epilabomenoi Simōna tina Kyrēnaion erchomenon apʼ agrou epethēkan autō ton stauron pherein opisthen tou Iēsou.

paragraphs.text: And there followed him a great multitude of the people, and of women who bewailed and lamented him.
paragraphs.original: Ἠκολούθει δὲ αὐτῷ πολὺ πλῆθος τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ γυναικῶν αἳ ἐκόπτοντο καὶ ἐθρήνουν αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: Ēkolouthei de autō poly plēthos tou laou kai gynaikōn hai ekoptonto kai ethrēnoun auton.

paragraphs.text: But Jesus turning unto them said, Daughters of Jerusalem, weep not for me, but weep for yourselves, and for your children.
paragraphs.original: στραφεὶς δὲ πρὸς αὐτὰς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Θυγατέρες Ἰερουσαλήμ, μὴ κλαίετε ἐπʼ ἐμέ· πλὴν ἐφʼ ἑαυτὰς κλαίετε καὶ ἐπὶ τὰ τέκνα ὑμῶν,
paragraphs.translit: strapheis de pros autas ho Iēsous eipen· Thygateres Ierousalēm, mē klaiete epʼ eme· plēn ephʼ heautas klaiete kai epi ta tekna hymōn,

paragraphs.text: For behold, the days are coming, in which they shall say, Blessed are the barren, and the wombs that never bare, and the breasts that never gave suck.
paragraphs.original: ὅτι ἰδοὺ ἔρχονται ἡμέραι ἐν αἷς ἐροῦσιν Μακάριαι αἱ στεῖραι καὶ αἱ κοιλίαι αἳ οὐκ ἐγέννησαν καὶ μαστοὶ οἳ οὐκ ἔθρεψαν.
paragraphs.translit: hoti idou erchontai hēmerai en hais erousin Makariai hai steirai kai hai koiliai hai ouk egennēsan kai mastoi hoi ouk ethrepsan.

paragraphs.text: Then shall they begin to say to the mountains, Fall on us; and to the hills, Cover us.
paragraphs.original: τότε ἄρξονται λέγειν τοῖς ὄρεσιν· Πέσετε ἐφʼ ἡμᾶς, καὶ τοῖς βουνοῖς· Καλύψατε ἡμᾶς·
paragraphs.translit: tote arxontai legein tois oresin· Pesete ephʼ hēmas, kai tois bounois· Kalypsate hēmas·

paragraphs.text: For if they do these things in the green tree, what shall be done in the dry?
paragraphs.original: ὅτι εἰ ἐν τῷ ὑγρῷ ξύλῳ ταῦτα ποιοῦσιν, ἐν τῷ ξηρῷ τί γένηται;
paragraphs.translit: hoti ei en tō hygrō xylō tauta poiousin, en tō xērō ti genētai;

paragraphs.text: And there were also two others, malefactors, led with him to be put to death.
paragraphs.original: Ἤγοντο δὲ καὶ ἕτεροι κακοῦργοι δύο σὺν αὐτῷ ἀναιρεθῆναι.
paragraphs.translit: Ēgonto de kai heteroi kakourgoi dyo syn autō anairethēnai.

paragraphs.text: And when they came unto the place which is called The skull, there they crucified him, and the malefactors, one on the right hand and the other on the left.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὅτε ἦλθον ἐπὶ τὸν τόπον τὸν καλούμενον Κρανίον, ἐκεῖ ἐσταύρωσαν αὐτὸν καὶ τοὺς κακούργους, ὃν μὲν ἐκ δεξιῶν ὃν δὲ ἐξ ἀριστερῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai hote ēlthon epi ton topon ton kaloumenon Kranion, ekei estaurōsan auton kai tous kakourgous, hon men ek dexiōn hon de ex aristerōn.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus said, Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do. And parting his garments among them, they cast lots.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἔλεγεν· Πάτερ, ἄφες αὐτοῖς, οὐ γὰρ οἴδασιν τί ποιοῦσιν. διαμεριζόμενοι δὲ τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ ἔβαλον κλήρους.
paragraphs.translit: ho de Iēsous elegen· Pater, aphes autois, ou gar oidasin ti poiousin. diamerizomenoi de ta himatia autou ebalon klērous.

paragraphs.text: And the people stood beholding. And the rulers also scoffed at him, saying, He saved others; let him save himself, if this is the Christ of God, his chosen.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἱστήκει ὁ λαὸς θεωρῶν. ἐξεμυκτήριζον δὲ καὶ οἱ ἄρχοντες λέγοντες· Ἄλλους ἔσωσεν, σωσάτω ἑαυτόν, εἰ οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ χριστὸς τοῦ θεοῦ, ὁ ἐκλεκτός.
paragraphs.translit: kai heistēkei ho laos theōrōn. exemyktērizon de kai hoi archontes legontes· Allous esōsen, sōsatō heauton, ei houtos estin ho christos tou theou, ho eklektos.

paragraphs.text: And the soldiers also mocked him, coming to him, offering him vinegar,
paragraphs.original: ἐνέπαιξαν δὲ αὐτῷ καὶ οἱ στρατιῶται προσερχόμενοι, ὄξος προσφέροντες αὐτῷ
paragraphs.translit: enepaixan de autō kai hoi stratiōtai proserchomenoi, oxos prospherontes autō

paragraphs.text: and saying, If thou art the King of the Jews, save thyself.
paragraphs.original: καὶ λέγοντες· Εἰ σὺ εἶ ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων, σῶσον σεαυτόν.
paragraphs.translit: kai legontes· Ei sy ei ho basileus tōn Ioudaiōn, sōson seauton.

paragraphs.text: And there was also a superscription over him, THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.
paragraphs.original: ἦν δὲ καὶ ἐπιγραφὴ ἐπʼ αὐτῷ· Ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων οὗτος.
paragraphs.translit: ēn de kai epigraphē epʼ autō· Ho basileus tōn Ioudaiōn houtos.

paragraphs.text: And one of the malefactors that were hanged railed on him, saying, Art not thou the Christ? save thyself and us.
paragraphs.original: Εἷς δὲ τῶν κρεμασθέντων κακούργων ἐβλασφήμει αὐτόν λέγων· Οὐχὶ σὺ εἶ ὁ χριστός; σῶσον σεαυτὸν καὶ ἡμᾶς.
paragraphs.translit: Heis de tōn kremasthentōn kakourgōn eblasphēmei auton legōn· Ouchi sy ei ho christos; sōson seauton kai hēmas.

paragraphs.text: But the other answered, and rebuking him said, Dost thou not even fear God, seeing thou art in the same condemnation?
paragraphs.original: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ ἕτερος ἐπιτιμῶν αὐτῷ ἔφη· Οὐδὲ φοβῇ σὺ τὸν θεόν, ὅτι ἐν τῷ αὐτῷ κρίματι εἶ;
paragraphs.translit: apokritheis de ho heteros epitimōn autō ephē· Oude phobē sy ton theon, hoti en tō autō krimati ei;

paragraphs.text: And we indeed justly; for we receive the due reward of our deeds: but this man hath done nothing amiss.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἡμεῖς μὲν δικαίως, ἄξια γὰρ ὧν ἐπράξαμεν ἀπολαμβάνομεν· οὗτος δὲ οὐδὲν ἄτοπον ἔπραξεν.
paragraphs.translit: kai hēmeis men dikaiōs, axia gar hōn epraxamen apolambanomen· houtos de ouden atopon epraxen.

paragraphs.text: And he said, Jesus, remember me when thou comest in thy kingdom.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἔλεγεν· Ἰησοῦ, μνήσθητί μου ὅταν ἔλθῃς ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ σου.
paragraphs.translit: kai elegen· Iēsou, mnēsthēti mou hotan elthēs en tē basileia sou.

paragraphs.text: And he said unto him, Verily I say unto thee, To-day shalt thou be with me in Paradise.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἀμήν σοι λέγω σήμερον μετʼ ἐμοῦ ἔσῃ ἐν τῷ παραδείσῳ.
paragraphs.translit: kai eipen autō· Amēn soi legō sēmeron metʼ emou esē en tō paradeisō.

paragraphs.text: And it was now about the sixth hour, and a darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour,
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἦν ἤδη ὡσεὶ ὥρα ἕκτη καὶ σκότος ἐγένετο ἐφʼ ὅλην τὴν γῆν ἕως ὥρας ἐνάτης
paragraphs.translit: Kai ēn ēdē hōsei hōra hektē kai skotos egeneto ephʼ holēn tēn gēn heōs hōras enatēs

paragraphs.text: the sun`s light failing: and the veil of the temple was rent in the midst.
paragraphs.original: τοῦ ἡλίου ἐκλιπόντος, ἐσχίσθη δὲ τὸ καταπέτασμα τοῦ ναοῦ μέσον.
paragraphs.translit: tou hēliou eklipontos, eschisthē de to katapetasma tou naou meson.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus, crying with a loud voice, said, Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit: and having said this, he gave up the ghost.
paragraphs.original: καὶ φωνήσας φωνῇ μεγάλῃ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Πάτερ, εἰς χεῖράς σου παρατίθεμαι τὸ πνεῦμά μου. τοῦτο δὲ εἰπὼν ἐξέπνευσεν.
paragraphs.translit: kai phōnēsas phōnē megalē ho Iēsous eipen· Pater, eis cheiras sou paratithemai to pneuma mou. touto de eipōn exepneusen.

paragraphs.text: And when the centurion saw what was done, he glorified God, saying, Certainly this was a righteous man.
paragraphs.original: Ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ ἑκατοντάρχης τὸ γενόμενον ἐδόξαζεν τὸν θεὸν λέγων· Ὄντως ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος δίκαιος ἦν.
paragraphs.translit: Idōn de ho hekatontarchēs to genomenon edoxazen ton theon legōn· Ontōs ho anthrōpos houtos dikaios ēn.

paragraphs.text: And all the multitudes that came together to this sight, when they beheld the things that were done, returned smiting their breasts.
paragraphs.original: καὶ πάντες οἱ συμπαραγενόμενοι ὄχλοι ἐπὶ τὴν θεωρίαν ταύτην, θεωρήσαντες τὰ γενόμενα, τύπτοντες τὰ στήθη ὑπέστρεφον.
paragraphs.translit: kai pantes hoi symparagenomenoi ochloi epi tēn theōrian tautēn, theōrēsantes ta genomena, typtontes ta stēthē hypestrephon.

paragraphs.text: And all his acquaintance, and the women that followed with him from Galilee, stood afar off, seeing these things.
paragraphs.original: εἱστήκεισαν δὲ πάντες οἱ γνωστοὶ αὐτῷ μακρόθεν, καὶ γυναῖκες αἱ συνακολουθοῦσαι αὐτῷ ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας, ὁρῶσαι ταῦτα.
paragraphs.translit: heistēkeisan de pantes hoi gnōstoi autō makrothen, kai gynaikes hai synakolouthousai autō apo tēs Galilaias, horōsai tauta.

paragraphs.text: And behold, a man named Joseph, who was a councillor, a good and righteous man
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ ὀνόματι Ἰωσὴφ βουλευτὴς ὑπάρχων, ἀνὴρ ἀγαθὸς καὶ δίκαιος—
paragraphs.translit: Kai idou anēr onomati Iōsēph bouleutēs hyparchōn, anēr agathos kai dikaios—

paragraphs.text: (he had not consented to their counsel and deed), [a man] of Arimathaea, a city of the Jews, who was looking for the kingdom of God:
paragraphs.original: οὗτος οὐκ ἦν συγκατατεθειμένος τῇ βουλῇ καὶ τῇ πράξει αὐτῶν— ἀπὸ Ἁριμαθαίας πόλεως τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ὃς προσεδέχετο τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: houtos ouk ēn synkatatetheimenos tē boulē kai tē praxei autōn— apo Harimathaias poleōs tōn Ioudaiōn, hos prosedecheto tēn basileian tou theou,

paragraphs.text: this man went to Pilate, and asked for the body of Jesus.
paragraphs.original: οὗτος προσελθὼν τῷ Πιλάτῳ ᾐτήσατο τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: houtos proselthōn tō Pilatō ētēsato to sōma tou Iēsou,

paragraphs.text: And he took it down, and wrapped it in a linen cloth, and laid him in a tomb that was hewn in stone, where never man had yet lain.
paragraphs.original: καὶ καθελὼν ἐνετύλιξεν αὐτὸ σινδόνι, καὶ ἔθηκεν αὐτὸν ἐν μνήματι λαξευτῷ οὗ οὐκ ἦν οὐδεὶς οὔπω κείμενος.
paragraphs.translit: kai kathelōn enetylixen auto sindoni, kai ethēken auton en mnēmati laxeutō hou ouk ēn oudeis oupō keimenos.

paragraphs.text: And it was the day of the Preparation, and the sabbath drew on.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἡμέρα ἦν παρασκευῆς, καὶ σάββατον ἐπέφωσκεν.
paragraphs.translit: kai hēmera ēn paraskeuēs, kai sabbaton epephōsken.

paragraphs.text: And the women, who had come with him out of Galilee, followed after, and beheld the tomb, and how his body was laid.
paragraphs.original: κατακολουθήσασαι δὲ αἱ γυναῖκες, αἵτινες ἦσαν συνεληλυθυῖαι ἐκ τῆς Γαλιλαίας αὐτῷ, ἐθεάσαντο τὸ μνημεῖον καὶ ὡς ἐτέθη τὸ σῶμα αὐτοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: katakolouthēsasai de hai gynaikes, haitines ēsan synelēlythyiai ek tēs Galilaias autō, etheasanto to mnēmeion kai hōs etethē to sōma autou,

paragraphs.text: And they returned, and prepared spices and ointments. And on the sabbath they rested according to the commandment.
paragraphs.original: ὑποστρέψασαι δὲ ἡτοίμασαν ἀρώματα καὶ μύρα. Καὶ τὸ μὲν σάββατον ἡσύχασαν κατὰ τὴν ἐντολήν,
paragraphs.translit: hypostrepsasai de hētoimasan arōmata kai myra. Kai to men sabbaton hēsychasan kata tēn entolēn,
